newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia tells "punks" to change or leave school.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia tells "punks" to change or leave school.

text.p: Malaysian students sporting spiky or dyed hair in the fashion of "punks" will have to adopt a more conservative hairstyle if they want to stay in school, Education Minister Najib Abdul Razak said on Monday.
Speaking on the television programme "Malaysia Today", Najib said he had ordered officials to investigate punk culture among students.
He said students with punk hairstyles would not be allowed to remain in school.
His comments followed newspaper articles last week in the Malay-language newspaper Utusan which described the growing popularity of the punk culture in Malaysia.
It said leather shirts and pants were becoming a chic form of punk and "pogo dancing", in which partners jump up and down and grab each other by the shirt, was also becoming popular.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, reacting to the articles last week, urged Malaysian youths to reject punk fashions and other "negative Western influences".
